title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Keep GDN prefill checkpoint metadata local to each cache group
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

In the GLM-5.3-Flash configuration we tested with Model Runner V2 (MRV2) and prefix caching, later requests could return garbled output despite succeeding. A **checkpoint**—attention state saved for prefix reuse—could be written to the wrong cache page. Found while testing [providers-verifier](https://github.com/smg-project/providers-verifier).

## Claims

- The [two-line fix](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/df28422b4d5be9314388a971952bdc614e13a292/vllm/v1/attention/backends/gdn_attn.py#L129-L139) makes checkpoint configurations use the runner's [existing per-group metadata construction](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/df28422b4d5be9314388a971952bdc614e13a292/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py#L523-L548).
- Configurations without checkpoint blocks still reuse metadata.
- Prefix caching and GLM's internal prefill checkpoint optimization from #56960 remain enabled: a full prefill can save an intermediate checkpoint without an extra model forward when the token budget permits.

## Validation

### Minimal reproducible example

Each **KV cache group** has its own cache-page mapping. When switching groups, [`update_block_table()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/df28422b4d5be9314388a971952bdc614e13a292/vllm/v1/attention/backends/gdn_attn.py#L613-L661) updates the active-state page but retains the previous group's checkpoint page:

| Page for the next cache group | Expected | Actual |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Active state | `202` | `202` |
| Checkpoint | `222` | **`111`** |

<details>
<summary>Minimal reproducible example — CPU Python script</summary>

Requires a configured vLLM Python environment with Torch. No GPU or model weights are needed.

```python
from types import SimpleNamespace

import torch

from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.checkpoint import MambaPrefillCheckpointMetadata
from vllm.v1.attention.backends.gdn_attn import (
    GDNAttentionMetadata,
    GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder,
)

title: [Bug]: GLM-5.3-Flash (Glm5Next): common non-square images (4032x3024, 3840x2160, A4 at 300 dpi) are refused with "exceeds the pre-allocated encoder cache size 7921"
bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

vLLM `0.28.1rc1.dev580+g385dce36b` (source commit 385dce36bcee42309924a5ece951a96db3dce7f2), `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` at revision `423acf37583782c51c142d145aef733d72943d93`, two DGX Spark (GB10) nodes, `max_num_batched_tokens` 2048, vision enabled (image only). The sizing code below is unchanged on main as of 4c2d277643e217344056e1d2c42115d5f005912f.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Valid images that the model's own processor accepts are rejected with HTTP 400:

```
The decoder prompt contains a(n) image item with 7950 embedding tokens, which exceeds the pre-allocated encoder cache size 7921. Please reduce the input size or increase the encoder cache size by setting --limit-mm-per-prompt at startup.
```

It is deterministic and it hits ordinary images. A typical phone photo (4032×3024), a 4K frame (3840×2160) and an A4 page at 300 dpi (3508×2480) all fail, while a square image of nearly the same size passes. Reproduced with generated images (script below), one request per image, `max_tokens` 8; the same seven results on two serving configurations:

| image | HTTP | tokens |
|---|---|---|
| 2560×1440 (QHD) | 200 | prompt 4,802 |
| 3000×3000 (square) | 200 | prompt 7,939 |
| 5000×2000 | 200 | prompt 7,858 |
| 4032×3024 (phone photo, 4:3) | **400** | image item 7,931 |
| 3840×2160 (4K, 16:9) | **400** | image item 7,973 |
| 3508×2480 (A4 at 300 dpi) | **400** | image item 7,950 |
| 2600×2400 | **400** | image item 7,998 |

(The accepted rows' prompt tokens are the image tokens plus 18 text tokens: 4,784, 7,921 and 7,840 image tokens.)

**Cause, as far as I can tell**

- The checkpoint's `processor_config.json` declares `max_image_tokens: 8000`, so the processor budget is `max_pixels = 8000 × 28 × 28 × 2 = 12,544,000`.
- The encoder cache is sized from `get_max_image_tokens()`, which uses `get_image_size_with_most_features()`. `Glm5NextProcessingInfo` (`vllm/models/glm5next/common/multimodal.py`) does not override it, so it inherits `Glm4vProc

title: [KV Offload] Give each rank its own CPU region outside the replicated layout
bodyExcerpt:
Outside the replicated layout, ranks never read each other's slots, but they still share one region whose rows interleave all ranks. Every rank pre-faults and pins its strided slots in the same shm file, contending with the others.

Give each rank its own region holding only its slots, in its own shm file. No other process maps that file, so the rank no longer waits on the cross-worker barrier before unlinking it. The replicated layout keeps the shared region.

## Tests

4× H200, measured on `16d4ac4ba3` with this change (the touched files are unchanged on current main):

- GLM-5.3 W4A8, TP4 + EP, 256 GiB native CPU offload: the offload startup step fell from 63.6 to 22.6 s (22.8 and 22.4 s in two runs), and pinning from 20.8 to 3.3 s. A 20k-token retrieval prompt answered 8/8 lookups cold and 8/8 after `/reset_prefix_cache`, with 3.9 GB reloaded from CPU.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_offload tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py`: 1182 passed. The 7 failing tests need a gated model and fail the same way on main.
- pre-commit, including mypy, passed.
author: Etelis

title: [KV Offload] Split the CPU offload region across shm files
bodyExcerpt:
Pre-faulting the CPU offload region is capped by its single `/dev/shm` file: page-cache inserts into one shmem file are serialized, so more workers or threads stop helping. On one H200 node, eight processes pre-faulting disjoint parts of a 64 GiB file reach 9.8 GiB/s in total. Given one file each, they reach 24.6 GiB/s, and sixteen files reach 44.8 GiB/s. #59430 hits the same ceiling with threads.

Split the region's rows over up to 32 files of at least 1 GiB each. The files are mapped back to back over one anonymous reservation, so the region stays contiguous. Workers with per-rank slots start pre-faulting on different files. Regions under 2 GiB, and other users of `SharedOffloadRegion`, keep a single file.

## Tests

4× H200, measured on `16d4ac4ba3` with this change (the touched files are unchanged on current main):

- GLM-5.3 W4A8, TP4 + EP, 256 GiB native CPU offload: the offload startup step fell from 63.6 to 38.3 s, and pre-faulting from 42.8 to 19.4 s. A 20k-token retrieval prompt answered 8/8 lookups cold and 8/8 after `/reset_prefix_cache`, with 3.9 GB reloaded from CPU.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_offload tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py`: 1183 passed. The 7 failing tests need a gated model and fail the same way on main.
- pre-commit, including mypy, passed.
author: Etelis

title: [KV Offload] Split replicated-layout pre-faulting across workers
bodyExcerpt:
With the replicated layout, every worker maps the same bytes, yet every worker still pre-faults the whole region. At TP4, that is four passes over one shm file, all contending for the same pages.

Give each worker one contiguous, page-aligned share to pre-fault instead. The pages are shared, so the region still ends up fully populated.

## Tests

4× H200, measured on `16d4ac4ba3` with this change (the touched files are unchanged on current main). GLM-5.3 only uses the replicated layout with #57652, so these runs have that PR applied:

- GLM-5.3 W4A8, TP4 + EP, 256 GiB native CPU offload: the offload startup step fell from 162.8 to 46.7 s. A 20k-token retrieval prompt answered 8/8 lookups cold and 8/8 after `/reset_prefix_cache`, with 3.9 GB reloaded from CPU.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_offload tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py`: 1184 passed. The 7 failing tests need a gated model and fail the same way on main.
- pre-commit, including mypy, passed.
author: Etelis

title: [KV Offload] Pin only each worker's own offload slots
bodyExcerpt:
Outside the replicated layout, each worker only uses its own slot of every row in the shared CPU region, yet every worker `cudaHostRegister`s the whole region. At TP4, every page gets pinned four times.

Register only the worker's slot of each row, rounded out to pages. The replicated layout keeps whole-region registration. So do slots within a page of the full row and regions over 65,536 rows, where per-call overhead would dominate.

TieringOffloadingSpec workers pin through the same path, so they get this too. #59430 lists this redundant pinning as a follow-up, and no open PR changes it.

## Tests

4× H200, measured on `16d4ac4ba3` with this change (the touched files are unchanged on current main):

- GLM-5.3 W4A8, TP4 + EP, 256 GiB native CPU offload: the offload startup step fell from 63.6 to 34.8 s, and pinning from 20.8 to 6.8 s, as each rank registered 68.8 GB instead of 274.9 GB. A 20k-token retrieval prompt answered 8/8 lookups cold and 8/8 after `/reset_prefix_cache`, with 3.9 GB reloaded from CPU.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_offload tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py`: 1184 passed. The 7 failing tests need a gated model and fail the same way on main.
- pre-commit, including mypy, passed.

title: [Core] Take the top-k/top-p Triton scratch from WorkspaceManager
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Take the per-program float32 scratch of `apply_top_k_top_p_triton` from `WorkspaceManager`, reserved at its maximum size by the GPU model runners before capture and the workspace lock. Part of #59055; with #59156 the memory is then released by `/sleep`.

## Claims

- The sampler scratch (`min(num_sm, batch) × vocab × 4 B`; 77 MiB per GPU on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, 92 MiB on GLM-5.3) no longer stays resident while the engine sleeps once #59156 lands, and no longer grows lazily under traffic after warm-up.
- Kernel behavior is unchanged: the same `(NUM_PROGRAMS, vocab)` float32 buffer is handed to `_topk_topp`.
- Callers without a reservation (CPU, tests, `diffusion_gemma`, the watermark sampler, batches larger than the reservation) keep the module-level cached buffer, so nothing can hit the workspace lock.

## Validation

- Unit tests (H200): `tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py`, `test_sampler.py`, `test_rejection_sampler.py`: 236 passed, 1 skipped, 7 failed; the 7 failures (`TestFlashInferDistributionMatch`, `No module named 'scipy'`) are identical on unmodified `main` in that environment.
- `pre-commit` (ruff, ruff format, mypy, etc.) passes on the commit.
- End-to-end, DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 with MTP, CUDA graphs and `--enable-sleep-mode` on 4× GB300, same image and node, on top of #59156 + #59158 + #59360:
  - Memory per GPU after `/sleep` (nvidia-smi): 6313/6439 MiB without this PR (an earlier 100-cycle run of the same stack on the same node, not a back-to-back A/B), 6023 MiB on all 4 GPUs with it. Only about 75 MiB of that is attributable to this change: torch-allocated memory outside the KV cache drops by 75 MiB (the lazily grown sampler buffer); the rest is caching-allocator reserved space (-162 MiB) and the +126 MiB the baseline shows on two GPUs from run to run.
  - Post-wake parity 0/0/0/0 MiB; 3 sleep/wake cycles (full, selective, full) with 195/195 outputs identical to the pre-sleep reference; no `Workspace is locked` errors.

title: [Core] Move FlashInfer MLA decode workspaces into WorkspaceManager
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Move the FlashInfer MLA decode workspaces (sparse trtllm-gen/cute-dsl, dense MLA, DSV4/DSV4.1 sparse) from module-global `torch.zeros` tensors into `WorkspaceManager` scratch. Part of #59055; with #59156 the memory is then released by `/sleep`.

## Claims

- The 394 MiB per GPU FlashInfer sparse-MLA workspace (GLM-5.3 / GLM-5.3-Flash) and the 128/256 MiB dense-MLA and DSV4 workspaces no longer stay resident while the engine sleeps once #59156 lands, and are no longer additive to the shared scratch while awake.
- No behavior change for the kernels: the buffers are requested at the same size, reserved before CUDA graph capture, and re-requested on every call (same pattern as `flashmla_sparse.py`, `prefill/trtllm_ragged.py`).
- The DCP sizing (`_required_workspace_bytes`) and `VLLM_FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BUFFER_SIZE` override are unchanged.

## Validation

- Read FlashInfer 0.7.0 (`mla/_core.py`, `data/csrc/trtllm_fmha_kernel_launcher.cu`, `cute_dsl/attention/{mla_decode.py,monolithic/mla_decode.py}`); 0.7.0.post1 (the pinned version) differs from 0.7.0 only in `aot.py`, `jit/gemm/core.py` and tests. On every decode path these backends use, the workspace holds only per-launch scratch (trtllm-gen: softmax-stats slab + split-KV scratch, semaphores live in the separate `multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer`; cute-dsl: split-KV `acc_o`/`acc_lse` partials consumed by the reduction kernel of the same call; SM120 sparse: `mid_out`/`mid_lse` partials), so no content survives between calls and no zero-init is needed. The prefill backends already hand trtllm-gen an uninitialized `WorkspaceManager` view.
- No other `WorkspaceManager` view is an input/output of these decode kernels on the paths read (inputs come from the persistent `topk_indices_buffer`, the index group, Triton converters, `_mtp_hidden_buffer`).
- Unit tests (H200, FlashInfer 0.6.12 venv): `tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_workspace.py`, `test_sparse_mla_backends.py`, `test_flashinfer_mla_dcp.py`,

title: [Bugfix] Keep the GLM-5.3 kpool tail and Qwen4 QSA ring out of the null block
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Block id 0 is the null block. It is shared by every KV cache group and is assumed to stay zero. Since #35431, the runners mark rows that own no state with 0 in the block table, not `PAD_SLOT_ID`: dummy runs, CUDA graph capture and padding rows all carry 0. Two ring caches that address their pages through column 0 of the block table did not treat 0 as "no ring", so dummy runs wrote their rows into block 0:

- **GLM-5.3-Flash kpool tail:** `_kpool_tail_slot_mapping_kernel` maps every token to `block_table[req][0] * kpool + pos % kpool`. Its torch fallback does the same.
- **Qwen4 QSA circular ring:** `circular_qsa_slot_mapping` and `_build_qsa_metadata_kernel` map tokens to `block_table[req, 0]` and kept every block `>= 0`. The compressed QSA path already keeps dummy slots inert (`test_qsa_compressed_metadata_keeps_dummy_slots_inert`); the ring path did not.

Every scheduled request owns its ring block, so a request on the null block has none. Its tokens now map to PAD, as the generic slot mapping does. The ring writers already skip PAD slots.

This is the same pattern as #58560, which fixes the DeepSeek-V4.1 compressor ring.

## Changes

- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`: the kpool tail slot mapping (Triton and torch) emits PAD for requests on the null block.
- `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/common/qsa_cache.py`: the QSA circular ring slot mapping (torch and Triton) requires block `> 0`.
- Tests: the existing QSA circular metadata test, which runs the Triton builder, also checks a dummy batch (all-zero block table) and expects PAD. QSA tests that used block 0 as a real ring block now start real blocks at 1. This includes `_make_block_table` in the pre-indexer test, which could randomly hand out block 0. The kpool tail change has no new test: its unit tests run the torch fallback on CPU, while production only takes the Triton kernel. It was checked by hand on both paths.

## Not a duplicate

- #58560 covers only the DeepSeek-V4.1 compressor ring.
